pictures.scene: Juarez, The Prayer in the Garden — Christ kneels on the dark ground of the olive garden in a rose coloured robe with a ring of gold light about His head and both hands opened out before Him, looking up at an angel who stands on the cloud above holding out a golden cup to Him, while one disciple lies asleep on the rocks below, one day in a place where jesus had just finished praying, one of his disciples requested, lord, teach us to pray, just as john taught his disciples, so jesus told them, when you pray, say, father, hallowed be your name, your kingdom come
pictures.name: pd_juarez_prayer_in_the_garden

pictures.scene: Steen, The Prayer before the Meal — a poor family in a bare room says grace before eating, the mother in a white cap holding her baby on her lap with her eyes shut, the father bent down over his folded hands with a child beside him, and a loaf, a wedge of butter and a dish of meat set out on the cloth in front of them, give us each day our daily bread, and forgive us our sins, for we also forgive everyone who sins against us, and lead us not into temptation
pictures.name: pd_steen_prayer_before_the_meal

pictures.scene: Van Schendel, The Night Market — a single candle burning in a basket of fish lights up two women out in the dark square long after nightfall, one standing with a pail on her arm and the other leaning forward in a wide cap to reach across the stall to her, with one street lantern glowing far off behind them, then jesus said to them, suppose one of you goes to his friend at midnight and says, friend, lend me three loaves of bread, because a friend of mine has come to me on a journey, and i have nothing to set before him
pictures.name: pd_schendel_nacht

pictures.scene: Maes, Young Woman by the Cradle — a young woman in a white collar sits up late in a dark shut room holding an open book on her knee and lifting one finger for quiet as she leans over a wicker cradle where a swaddled baby lies fast asleep under a red blanket, and suppose the one inside answers, do not bother me, my door is already shut, and my children and i are in bed, i cannot get up to give you anything, i tell you, even though he will not get up to provide for him because of his friendship, yet because of the man's persistence, he will get up and give him as much as he needs
pictures.name: pd_maes_jonge_vrouw_bij_de_wieg

pictures.scene: Bauernfeind, A Street in Jerusalem — a narrow cobbled street of honey coloured stone runs in under a great pointed archway hung with lamps, with latticed windows and awnings leaning out overhead and townspeople coming and going through the gate in the hot sunlight, a boy with his dog in the middle of the road and traders sitting out by their stalls, so i tell you, ask, and it will be given to you, seek, and you will find, knock, and the door will be opened to you, for everyone who asks receives, he who seeks finds, and to him who knocks, the door will be opened
pictures.name: pd_bauernfeind_jerusalem_gate

pictures.scene: Blommers, The Fisherman's Children — a barefoot boy in a dark smock sits on a basket at a scrubbed deal table in a poor brick room and holds up the little boat he has whittled, looking across at his sister, who has stopped her sewing with the needle still in her hand to look back at him, what father among you, if his son asks for a fish, will give him a snake instead, or if he asks for an egg, will give him a scorpion
pictures.name: pd_blommers_kinderen_van_de_visser

pictures.scene: El Greco, The Pentecost — a white dove comes down in a burst of gold light at the top of a tall shadowed room and sends out a crowded ring of small flames that stand burning over the heads of the apostles below, while the Virgin in a blue veil lifts her joined hands in the middle of them and every face around her turns up into the light, so if you who are evil know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your father in heaven give the holy spirit to those who ask him, one day jesus was driving out a demon that was mute, and when the demon was gone, the man who had been mute spoke, the crowds were amazed
pictures.name: pd_el_greco_pentecost

pictures.scene: Rembrandt, The Woman Taken in Adultery — a shaft of light falls on a kneeling woman in white at the foot of a great dark temple, with Christ standing barefoot before her in a dull red robe and opening one hand as the elders press in around her in furs and gold turbans to put their charge to Him, while a whole crowd watches down from the lit gallery behind, but some of them said, it is by beelzebul, the prince of the demons, that he drives out demons, and others tested him by demanding a sign from heaven
pictures.name: pd_rembrandt_adulteress

pictures.scene: Cole, The Destruction of Empire — a great marble city turns on itself under a towering storm of smoke and cloud, its colonnades burning along both shores while an enemy army pours across the broken bridge in a seething mass of spears and banners, ships go down in the green harbour below and one woman in white runs out along the shattered parapet in the corner, knowing their thoughts, jesus said to them, every kingdom divided against itself will be laid waste, and a house divided against a house will fall, if satan is divided against himself, how can his kingdom stand, after all, you say that i drive out demons by beelzebul
pictures.name: pd_cole_destruction

pictures.scene: Domenichino, Moses and the Burning Bush — a shepherd in a red cloak sits down among his sheep on the bank of a wide blue lake and throws one arm up over his head to shade his eyes as he stares across at a low thorn bush standing in a sheet of pale flame that does not consume it, with great trees overhead and a walled town and blue mountains lying far off across the water, and if i drive out demons by beelzebul, by whom do your sons drive them out, so then, they will be your judges, but if i drive out demons by the finger of god, then the kingdom of god has come upon you
pictures.name: pd_domenichino_burning_bush

pictures.scene: Rembrandt, A Man in Armour — a young soldier in a tall golden helmet with a plume stands out of a brown darkness in profile, his steel breastplate and shoulder pieces catching the light and a heavy crimson cloak hanging down behind his arm, while he lowers his eyes and holds a shield steady at his side, when a strong man, fully armed, guards his house, his possessions are secure, but when someone stronger attacks and overpowers him, he takes away the armor in which the man trusted, and then he divides up his plunder
pictures.name: pd_rembrandt_man_armour

pictures.scene: Church, Twilight in the Wilderness — a whole sky of torn red and crimson cloud burns out over an empty mountain country at the last of the light, with a band of clear yellow lying along the ridges on the horizon and a still dark lake below holding the colour in its water, and not one person anywhere in the land, he who is not with me is against me, and he who does not gather with me scatters, when an unclean spirit comes out of a man, it passes through arid places seeking rest and does not find it, then it says, i will return to the house i left
pictures.name: pd_church_twilight_in_the_wilderness

pictures.scene: Hammershoi, Interior with a Young Woman Seen from Behind — a young woman in a plain long black dress stands with her back to us in a swept and perfectly bare grey room, setting down a white dish on the edge of a polished table under an empty wall where a single picture frame hangs just inside the corner, and nothing else at all in the room with her, on its return, it finds the house swept clean and put in order, then it goes and brings seven other spirits more wicked than itself, and they go in and dwell there, and the final plight of that man is worse than the first
pictures.name: pd_hammershoi_interieur

pictures.scene: Neuhuys, Mother and Child — a young peasant mother in a white cap and a worn brown jacket sits on a rush chair against the bare wall of a poor cottage with her baby held up on her lap in a little white shift, steadying its bare legs with one hand while the child turns a spoon over in its fingers and she looks down into its face, with a basket of mending set out on the table beside them, as jesus was saying these things, a woman in the crowd raised her voice and said, blessed is the womb that bore you, and blessed are the breasts that nursed you, but he replied, blessed rather are those who hear the word of god and obey it
pictures.name: pd_neuhuys_moeder_en_kind

pictures.scene: Rosa, Jonah Preaching to the Ninevites — a prophet in a white turban and a pale robe stands up among the columns of a great city at evening and throws both arms wide open as he cries out his warning, while the people of the town go down all round him under a dark storming sky, one woman kneeling with her hand lifted toward him and an old man clasping his hands at his feet, as the crowds were increasing, jesus said, this is a wicked generation, it demands a sign, but none will be given it except the sign of jonah, for as jonah was a sign to the ninevites, so the son of man will be a sign to this generation
pictures.name: pd_rosa_jonah

pictures.scene: Poynter, The Visit of the Queen of Sheba to Solomon — a bearded king in a white embroidered mantle and a gold crown comes down a flight of marble steps lined with gilded lions and holds out his open hand in welcome, with harpers playing below him, his guards standing among the great red and gold pillars of the hall, and the women of the court watching from their couches along the terrace, the queen of the south will rise at the judgment with the men of this generation and condemn them, for she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of solomon, and now one greater than solomon is here, the men of nineveh will stand at the judgment with this generation and condemn it, for they repented at the preaching of jonah, and now one greater than jonah is here
pictures.name: pd_poynter_queen_of_sheba

pictures.scene: Dou, The Night School — one candle standing up in a brass holder on a plain table is the only light in a black room, and every face in the school leans in toward it, a girl reading her page across the table, the master bending over with his pen out above an hourglass, a woman holding up a second small flame at the left and a boy crouched under her with a slate on his knees, no one lights a lamp and puts it in a cellar or under a basket, instead, he sets it on a stand, so those who enter can see the light, your eye is the lamp of your body, when your eyes are good, your whole body also is full of light, but when they are bad, your body is full of darkness
pictures.name: pd_dou_night_school

pictures.scene: Correggio, The Holy Night — the newborn child lying in His mother's arms on the straw is Himself the only light in the stable, and the glow off Him strikes up into her bent face and out across the shepherds crowding in at the left, one of them throwing up a hand against the brightness and another kneeling in beside the manger with his staff, while the ox and the ass stand in the dark behind, be careful, then, that the light within you is not darkness, so if your whole body is full of light, with no part of it in darkness, you will be radiant, as though a lamp were shining on you
pictures.name: pd_correggio_holy_night

pictures.scene: Perov, The Monastery Refectory — a rich lady in a lilac silk gown sweeps into a vaulted monastery hall on the arm of an old official with a star on his coat, and the black robed monks bow and spread their hands to usher her forward while one of them lies flat on the stones at her feet, as a beggar woman on the floor in the corner lifts both hands to her with two ragged children beside her and nobody turns round, as jesus was speaking, a pharisee invited him to dine with him, so he went in and reclined at the table, but the pharisee was surprised to see that jesus did not first wash before the meal
pictures.name: pd_perov_kloostermaaltijd

pictures.scene: Zurbaran, Still Life with Vessels — two earthenware jars stand side by side on a bare shelf out of a deep black ground, a wide pale green pitcher with two looped handles and a scalloped lip scoured clean on the outside, and a narrow red clay flask beside it with a long ringed neck, and nothing in the picture but the light lying along their polished sides, now then, said the lord, you pharisees clean the outside of the cup and dish, but inside you are full of greed and wickedness, you fools, did not the one who made the outside make the inside as well
pictures.name: pd_zurbaran_kruiken

pictures.scene: Beuckelaer, The Vegetable Market — a market woman in a white smock and a red laced bodice sits in behind a timber stall banked high with produce and reaches out both hands over it, steadying a little basket of white herbs with one and a great round basket of artichokes, cherries and currants with the other, with pears, apples and plums heaped in flat baskets at her shoulder and cabbages and melons piled all along the front, but give as alms the things that are within you, and you will see that everything is clean for you, woe to you pharisees, you pay tithes of mint, rue, and every herb, but you disregard justice and the love of god, you should have practiced the latter without neglecting the former
pictures.name: pd_beuckelaer_groentemarkt

pictures.scene: Ruisdael, The Jewish Cemetery — white marble tombs stand out in a rough overgrown burying ground below the broken tower of a ruined church, with a great dead tree fallen across the foreground and a stream running down over the stones past it, storm cloud driving across the whole sky above and a faint rainbow showing through the rain at the left, woe to you pharisees, you love the chief seats in the synagogues and the greetings in the marketplaces, woe to you, for you are like unmarked graves, which men walk over without even noticing
pictures.name: pd_ruisdael_the_jewish_cemetery

pictures.scene: Jarnefelt, Under the Yoke — a thin girl in a torn white shirt and a sack coloured skirt stands up out of the smoke of a burning clearing with her face smeared black and her eyes red, holding a long heavy pole in both hands and looking straight out at us, while a man in a white smock works on through the smoke behind her among the smouldering stumps, one of the experts in the law told him, teacher, when you say these things, you insult us as well, woe to you as well, experts in the law, he replied, you weigh men down with heavy burdens, but you yourselves will not lift a finger to lighten their load
pictures.name: pd_jarnefelt_zwoegers

pictures.scene: Gerome, Solomon's Wall in Jerusalem — an immense wall of ancient honey coloured blocks rises up out of the frame in the afternoon sun with tufts of dry hyssop sprouting from every joint in the stone, and a handful of worshippers stand along the foot of it with their faces pressed against the masonry, one in a white robe, one barefoot in a dark cloak, and a man in a fur hat waiting back on the flagstones behind them, woe to you, you build tombs for the prophets, but it was your fathers who killed them, so you are witnesses consenting to the deeds of your fathers, they killed the prophets, and you build their tombs
pictures.name: pd_gerome_the_wall_of_solomon

pictures.scene: Surikov, The Morning of the Streltsy Execution — condemned men sit in carts in the churned mud of a great city square at first light, each holding a lit candle in his bound hands, one in a white shirt staring out, one black bearded and unbowed in a red coat, while their wives and mothers wail on the ground around the wheels, a little girl in a red kerchief clinging to her mother's skirt, and the painted domes of the cathedral standing up behind the packed crowd, because of this, the wisdom of god said, i will send them prophets and apostles, some of them they will kill and others they will persecute, as a result, this generation will be charged with the blood of all the prophets that has been shed since the foundation of the world
pictures.name: pd_surikov_the_morning_of_the_streltsy_execution

pictures.scene: Victors, Hannah Praying in the Temple — an old woman in a wide red and gold headdress and a heavy fur trimmed robe stands close up against a dark stone pier inside the temple court with her hands locked tightly together in front of her, lifting her worn face and her brimming eyes up and away to one side and moving her lips without a sound, from the blood of abel to the blood of zechariah, who was killed between the altar and the sanctuary, yes, i tell you, all of it will be charged to this generation, woe to you experts in the law, for you have taken away the key to knowledge, you yourselves have not entered, and you have hindered those who were entering
pictures.name: pd_victors_hanna_biddend_in_de_tempel

pictures.scene: Durer, Christ Among the Doctors — a boy in a blue green robe with a faint ring of light behind His head stands hemmed in on every side by learned old men pressing their open books and codices at Him, and in the middle of the picture His slender hands and the knotted bony hands of the oldest doctor are locked together in the air, ticking the argument off finger by finger while the old man leans in snarling into His ear, as jesus went on from there, the scribes and pharisees began to oppose him bitterly and to ply him with questions about many things, waiting to catch him in something he might say
pictures.name: pd_durer_doctors

lines.text: One day in a place where Jesus had just finished praying, one of His disciples requested, Lord, teach us to pray, just as John taught his disciples.
So Jesus told them, When you pray, say: Father, hallowed be Your name. Your kingdom come.
Give us each day our daily bread.
And forgive us our sins, for we also forgive everyone who sins against us. And lead us not into temptation.
Then Jesus said to them, Suppose one of you goes to his friend at midnight and says, Friend, lend me three loaves of bread,
because a friend of mine has come to me on a journey, and I have nothing to set before him.
And suppose the one inside answers, Do not bother me. My door is already shut, and my children and I are in bed. I cannot get up to give you anything.
I tell you, even though he will not get up to provide for him because of his friendship, yet because of the man's persistence, he will get up and give him as much as he needs.
So I tell you: Ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and the door will be opened to you.
For everyone who asks receives; he who seeks finds; and to him who knocks, the door will be opened.
What father among you, if his son asks for a fish, will give him a snake instead?
Or if he asks for an egg, will give him a scorpion?
So if you who are evil know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father in heaven give the Holy Spirit to those who ask Him!
One day Jesus was driving out a demon that was mute. And when the demon was gone, the man who had been mute spoke. The crowds were amazed,
but some of them said, It is by Beelzebul, the prince of the demons, that He drives out demons.
And others tested Him by demanding a sign from heaven.
Knowing their thoughts, Jesus said to them, Every kingdom divided against itself will be laid waste, and a house divided against a house will fall.
If Satan is divided against himself, how can his kingdom stand? After all, you say that I drive out demons by Beelzebul.
And if I drive out demons by Beelzebul, by whom do your sons drive them out? So then, they will be your judges.
But if I drive out demons by the finger of God, then the kingdom of God has come upon you.
When a strong man, fully armed, guards his house, his possessions are secure.
But when someone stronger attacks and overpowers him, he takes away the armor in which the man trusted, and then he divides up his plunder.
He who is not with Me is against Me, and he who does not gather with Me scatters.
When an unclean spirit comes out of a man, it passes through arid places seeking rest and does not find it. Then it says, I will return to the house I left.
On its return, it finds the house swept clean and put in order.
Then it goes and brings seven other spirits more wicked than itself, and they go in and dwell there. And the final plight of that man is worse than the first.
As Jesus was saying these things, a woman in the crowd raised her voice and said, Blessed is the womb that bore You, and blessed are the breasts that nursed You!
But He replied, Blessed rather are those who hear the word of God and obey it.
As the crowds were increasing, Jesus said, This is a wicked generation. It demands a sign, but none will be given it except the sign of Jonah.
For as Jonah was a sign to the Ninevites, so the Son of Man will be a sign to this generation.

The Queen of the South will rise at the judgment with the men of this generation and condemn them; for she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon, and now One greater than Solomon is here.
The men of Nineveh will stand at the judgment with this generation and condemn it; for they repented at the preaching of Jonah, and now One greater than Jonah is here.
No one lights a lamp and puts it in a cellar or under a basket. Instead, he sets it on a stand, so those who enter can see the light.
Your eye is the lamp of your body. When your eyes are good, your whole body also is full of light. But when they are bad, your body is full of darkness.
Be careful, then, that the light within you is not darkness.
So if your whole body is full of light, with no part of it in darkness, you will be radiant, as though a lamp were shining on you.
As Jesus was speaking, a Pharisee invited Him to dine with him; so He went in and reclined at the table.
But the Pharisee was surprised to see that Jesus did not first wash before the meal.
Now then, said the Lord, you Pharisees clean the outside of the cup and dish, but inside you are full of greed and wickedness.
You fools! Did not the One who made the outside make the inside as well?
But give as alms the things that are within you, and you will see that everything is clean for you.
Woe to you Pharisees! You pay tithes of mint, rue, and every herb, but you disregard justice and the love of God. You should have practiced the latter without neglecting the former.
Woe to you Pharisees! You love the chief seats in the synagogues and the greetings in the marketplaces.
Woe to you! For you are like unmarked graves, which men walk over without even noticing.
One of the experts in the law told Him, Teacher, when You say these things, You insult us as well.
Woe to you as well, experts in the law! He replied. You weigh men down with heavy burdens, but you yourselves will not lift a finger to lighten their load.
Woe to you! You build tombs for the prophets, but it was your fathers who killed them.
So you are witnesses consenting to the deeds of your fathers: They killed the prophets, and you build their tombs.
Because of this, the wisdom of God said, I will send them prophets and apostles; some of them they will kill and others they will persecute.
As a result, this generation will be charged with the blood of all the prophets that has been shed since the foundation of the world,
from the blood of Abel to the blood of Zechariah, who was killed between the altar and the sanctuary. Yes, I tell you, all of it will be charged to this generation.
Woe to you experts in the law! For you have taken away the key to knowledge. You yourselves have not entered, and you have hindered those who were entering.
As Jesus went on from there, the scribes and Pharisees began to oppose Him bitterly and to ply Him with questions about many things,
waiting to catch Him in something He might say.
